I guess I just dont understand this. The point of having the follow up speech by the opposing party is to discuss what was just said in the SOTU address, yet it never does. The opposing party says, what that person said is wrong and then spews talking points for 15 minutes. This is not right vs left, this is tired of being fed the same crap. I thought she gave a great speech. I agreed with most of what she said. Even with that, what is the point? Its like we allow the opposing party to have a 10 minute commercial after the SOTU. If they are not going to discuss anything the president says, what is the point?
Why does the opposing party get to make rebuttal comments when they do not address any of the points called out in the state of the union?

First, the response to the SotU is usually paid by the opposition party, it's not a constitutional obligation - there's no formula, no protocols, etc. It's a publicity stunt since it first happened in 1966 and basically a way for the opposition to get some time in the limelight when all the eyes in the country are on the President. So they get to do it because they want to and pay for it.

In order to a proper rebuttal to be made the opposition would need to know the speech before (and not just a couple snippets that they release to the press, usually from the less important parts in order to not give ammo to the opposition) or have a massive task-force of fact-checkers disassembling each line of the speech in real time and rapidly assembling a counter-speech on the go - this is frankly not doable in able time for it to be an effective rebuttal, they'd need to at least to it overnight - which is bad in politics because you want your rebuttal done and out in the wild before the SotU is forgotten (which it'll be after the next day unless it's one of those memorable speeches in a dramatic moment of History) and that means before the newspapers are out and the news cycle of the next day has begun. These days it's even more important to be quick thanks to the internet and social media, so taking your time isn't much of an option.

So their best bet is to try to guess what the President will say or make a speech on things that they believe are not right and the president will likely try to mask or not mention - and in an election year, this will double as a tool to promote the opposition party platform.

Could it be delivered in a more effective way? Sure, in 1972 congressmen did a q&a question where people called-in and asked questions about the SotU, which would be cool but likely not a really good choice for practical reasons. The reality of time is that the speech ends late night, East Coast people will be soon going to bed since they need to wake up early next day, so it's better to say something quick that shows another view of the challenges the country face rather than to try a long, direct take-down that will take a huge effort to create and a good part of the country not will watch, care or talk about.
